title: Claude 3D Model Showcase
author: 314t
selftext: Just sharing all the assets claude has been making. What does everyone else's pipeline look like for making consistent assets? I've been using a skill to generate these, but still experimenting to get claude to build these faster and more efficiently. On over it can take claude 2-4 hours to make on asset, and token usage is heavy.  So far, I've noticed that the efforts are like thinking budgets, if you try to fit a long list of things into a low effort budget, then quality degrades, it misses things. So I've been experiment with various sonnet, haiku, opus agents at different levels. Still the best quality comes from a high or xhigh research agent, and a low build agent, with the build agent calling its own critic agents to tell it whats wrong, but still pretty token heavy. Any thoughts or suggestions?

replies.author: dilberry
replies.body:
Starting to sound like a paid shill, or bot I think.

Saying a lot, well saying nothing at all? There’s literally no advantage just spending 100 hours making 10 models with AI doing all of the modelling and iterating over and over again, and then calling making the same thing with the Superior product in a fraction of the time and a fraction of the cost “sloppy”?

I’d love to know how it’s sloppy to simply use a better product for the job. If you really wanna get into it, you can make these models piece by piece individually in either platform, and then have AI piece them together for your final product. In fact, I bet you dollars to donuts that if you asked Claude or ChatGPT, what the best route is, both of them would suggest that you should use the online platforms for modeling.

replies.author: Ok_Feedback4200
replies.body:
10+ years working in 3D, not bot, not paid by anyone to chat here..

100 hours for 10 models isn't great but this is just his experiments. Personally, I work in a bit of a different way while creating my game assets, but I still do it in a more traiditional way - directing my agent so it does this work the way it's supposed to be done, so I know topology, UVs, normals and overall style match what I want. If I didn't know how to sculpt, I'd probably use tripo for that too. For organic models, this can be the way to go for people creating these assets without sculpting knowledge and it will be better than trying to model it. But using it for every single asset, especially complex machinery? I don't think so...

Tripo or Meshy gives you a mess of a 3d scan that it later tries to make sense of while doing retopo. Retopo will not give you perfect topology. It can get you up to around 80%. For organic models, this matters less.

If you are so sure about your tripo being a better product, go ahead, try modeling enigma machine with it.. In a way that you can actually interact with it. Let's see how many hours and dollars you spend trying to recreate it...

replies.author: dilberry
replies.body: Ok, I hear your point but who is making enigma machines for their games here? The guy has models of sandstone walls and low poly villagers ffs... come on... Are we modeling the center of the universe by hand next? Or the entire DNA structure of a lizard?

replies.author: Ok_Feedback4200
replies.body: Ok, what about the cabinets if you want them open? A fridge with all the insides? Etc?... You get the idea.. It's the same as looking at modeling vs sculpting in the traditional 3D sense... We model hard surfaces and machines. We sculpt organic stuff... Tripo isn't modeling anything, it's much closer to sculpting. I know it has that new feature to break down moedl into pieces but it's also kept under most expensive sub and it's probably still shit when you need many different parts being modeled exactly with clean and straight edges, close to each other, etc... You won't get that precision from tripo.

replies.author: dilberry
replies.body:
Wrong though, and it sounds like you've never used Tripo.

If you want to model a face to animate, Tripo will create a full functioning head/face with eye balls, eye lids, lips, teeth, and tongue - all you need to do is give it a head reference shot with the mouth ever so slightly open and it will do the rest. 

If I wanted a fridge that opens and closes, I'd either model the fridge with the doors open then split the doors into moving parts to close, or model it twice open and closed) then animate the transition. 

Tripo/Meshy and any LLM are going to be dogshit compared to hand modeling like you suggest for a finished product and flexibility.

replies.author: Ok_Feedback4200
replies.body: Also... I make my own stylized assets. It takes my agent around 5min per model now to do first iteration. usually it's about 80% there. One more prompt and it will get fixed. And it will be made properly with all the separate parts right away, perfect topology the way I want... Then another prompt with another software and I can get it properly textured... You bet your ass my models will be better and made faster and cleaner this way than they would be in tripo. But at the same time I wouldn't ask my agent to model me a 3D character. I'd either sculpt it or go to tripo if I didn't know how to sculpt...

replies.author: dilberry
replies.body: Sorry but I don't believe it. There is no chance at all you have any LLM modeling in Blender making things anywhere near what Tripo or Meshy can spit out in 20-30 seconds without involving local models like Trellis.2, Hunyuan 3d, etc or calling APIs to different services.
